about: Native-integration capabilities of the framework versions used in this repository. 'docs' cells cite upstream documentation or release notes; 'repo' cells are backed by this repository's lockfiles, examples, captures or runner checks. Light/dark following was tested on GitHub runners by switching the OS to dark mode and relaunching each example. Other capabilities describe the current upstream release line; the Linux runs used Ubuntu 24.04's GTK 4.14 and Qt 6.4. The Dock, taskbar, tray, shortcut and launch rows are from documentation and crate sources.

frameworks.name: egui / eframe
frameworks.model: Immediate mode; draws its own widgets with OpenGL or wgpu
strengths: Very little code for tool-style UIs; state lives in plain Rust fields
Screen-reader support through AccessKit on all three systems
limits: Same custom look on every OS
Menus, tray, dialogs and notifications come from separate crates
Did not follow dark mode on Linux X11

frameworks.name: GTK4
frameworks.model: Retained widget tree styled by the GTK theme (Adwaita)
strengths: Native look and system integration on GNOME/Linux
Mature text stack (Pango) with bidi and IME
Smallest executables here; the GTK runtime is separate
limits: Looks like GTK, not like Windows or macOS
Did not follow system dark mode on any runner
Windows/macOS screen-reader backend is new and opt-in
No tray icon API; runtime must be bundled on Windows/macOS

frameworks.name: Slint
frameworks.model: Declarative .slint markup compiled to native code; own renderer
frameworks.license: GPL-3.0, royalty-free with attribution, or commercial
strengths: Smallest measured memory on every system
Followed system dark mode on all three runners
Built-in tray icon and native menu bar on Windows/macOS
limits: Drag and drop works only inside the app in 1.17–1.18
No built-in file dialog or notifications
Read the licence options before shipping closed-source

frameworks.name: Qt Widgets
frameworks.language: C++ here; Rust only via bridges such as CXX-Qt
frameworks.model: Retained C++ widget tree drawn with platform styles
strengths: Closest to native controls on Windows and macOS
Broadest built-in OS integration: dialogs, tray, menus, accessibility
Low measured memory on all three systems
limits: C++ API; Rust bindings target QML rather than Widgets
LGPL obligations or a commercial licence

frameworks.name: Tauri
frameworks.model: System webview (WebView2, WKWebView, WebKitGTK) driven by Rust
strengths: Any web UI stack; official plugins for dialogs, notifications, updates
Built-in bundler for installers on all three systems
limits: Highest measured memory on Linux and Windows: the webview runs extra processes
Different browser engine on each OS
Dark mode needs the app’s own CSS

features.title: Native-looking controls
features.description: Do buttons, lists and inputs look like the platform's own controls?

egui.note: egui draws its own style, identical on every OS.

gtk.note: Native on GNOME. On Windows and macOS it keeps the GTK theme rather than platform controls.

slint.note: Built-in styles imitate Fluent, Cupertino and Material; the native style renders through Qt when the Qt backend is used. Controls are drawn by Slint.

qt.note: Platform styles on Windows and macOS; on Linux the look depends on the desktop's Qt platform theme (Fusion by default).

tauri.note: Layout and styling come from the app's CSS. Form controls and scrollbars follow the webview's defaults.

features.title: Follows system light/dark
features.description: Tested: the OS was switched to dark mode and each example relaunched.

egui.note: Followed the OS on Windows and macOS (ThemePreference::System). On Linux X11 it stayed light although the Settings portal reported prefer-dark.

gtk.note: Stayed light on every runner: GTK 4.24 on Windows/macOS and GTK 4.14 with the Linux portal set to prefer-dark. GTK 4.20+ documents gtk-interface-color-scheme for Linux; libadwaita apps follow the portal.

slint.note: The std-widgets style switched to dark on Windows, macOS and Linux (portal).

qt.note: Switched on macOS (Qt 6.12). Stayed light on Windows Server 2022 with Qt 6.8.3 and on Linux with Qt 6.4, which predates QStyleHints::colorScheme (6.5).

tauri.note: All three webviews reported prefers-color-scheme: dark. The app must style dark mode itself; the example defines both palettes in CSS.

features.title: Native Wayland and X11
features.description: Runs natively on both Linux display protocols.

egui.note: Through winit. The measured example enables only the x11 feature on Linux.

gtk.note: Wayland and X11 backends are part of GTK.

slint.note: Through winit, plus a LinuxKMS backend without a compositor.

qt.note: Wayland and xcb platform plugins.

tauri.note: Through GTK3 and WebKitGTK.

features.title: Translucent window materials
features.description: Mica or Acrylic on Windows, vibrancy or Liquid Glass on macOS.

egui.note: window-vibrancy crate on a transparent viewport. Linux blur is up to the compositor.

gtk.note: No API; GTK draws an opaque surface. Linux blur is up to the compositor.

slint.note: window-vibrancy through the winit window handle.

qt.note: No Qt API; DwmSetWindowAttribute or NSVisualEffectView from native code.

tauri.note: windowEffects: Mica, Acrylic, Tabbed on Windows; vibrancy materials and Liquid Glass on macOS; unsupported on Linux.

features.title: Screen readers
features.description: Exposes the UI to Narrator/NVDA, VoiceOver and Orca.

egui.note: AccessKit adapters for Windows, macOS and AT-SPI are in the pinned lockfile (eframe feature accesskit).

gtk.note: AT-SPI on Linux. GTK 4.18 added an AccessKit backend for Windows/macOS; it is enabled at build time and selected with GTK_A11Y=accesskit.

slint.note: AccessKit adapters for all three systems are in the pinned lockfile (feature accessibility).

qt.note: UI Automation, NSAccessibility and AT-SPI.

tauri.note: Provided by the system webview; quality depends on the app's HTML semantics.

features.title: Input methods (CJK, dead keys)
features.description: Composes text through the OS input method.

egui.note: IME events through winit.

gtk.note: GtkIMContext with platform modules (IBus/Wayland text-input, Win32 IMM, macOS).

slint.note: IME events through winit.

qt.note: QInputMethod with platform input contexts.

tauri.note: Handled by the webview.

features.title: Right-to-left and bidi text
features.description: Arabic/Hebrew shaping, bidi reordering and mirrored layouts.

egui.note: Bidi shaping and RTL layout are open pull requests after 0.37.

gtk.note: Pango shaping and bidi; widgets mirror with the text direction.

slint.note: The pinned lockfile includes Parley and unicode-bidi for shaping. Automatic layout mirroring was not verified.

qt.note: Text shaping plus Qt::RightToLeft layout direction.

tauri.note: HTML dir and CSS logical properties.

features.title: Native menu bar
features.description: Uses the macOS global menu bar and native Windows menus.

egui.note: No menu-bar integration; the muda crate can add native menus.

gtk.note: gtk_application_set_menubar uses the macOS menu bar; elsewhere it is an in-window GTK menu.

slint.note: MenuBar uses the macOS menu bar and native Windows menus (muda, since 1.10); on Linux it is drawn by Slint.

qt.note: QMenuBar maps to the macOS global menu bar.

tauri.note: Native window and app menus (muda).

features.title: System tray icon
features.description: Notification-area or menu-bar status icon with a menu.

egui.note: Not built in; the tray-icon crate is the usual choice.

gtk.note: GtkStatusIcon was removed in GTK4.

slint.note: SystemTrayIcon since 1.17. Linux uses StatusNotifierItem; plain X11 trays are not supported.

qt.note: QSystemTrayIcon.

tauri.note: Core API behind the tray-icon feature.

features.title: Native file dialogs
features.description: Open/save dialogs provided by the OS or desktop portal.

egui.note: Not built in; rfd provides native dialogs.

gtk.note: GtkFileDialog uses Win32/macOS dialogs and the XDG portal.

slint.note: Not built in; rfd is commonly used.

qt.note: QFileDialog uses native dialogs by default.

tauri.note: tauri-plugin-dialog.

features.title: Desktop notifications
features.description: Toasts in the OS notification centre.

egui.note: Not built in; notify-rust or platform crates.

gtk.note: GNotification through GApplication; Linux uses the portal or freedesktop service. Windows/macOS backends were not verified.

slint.note: Not built in.

qt.note: Qt Widgets has no notification-centre API; QSystemTrayIcon::showMessage shows a tray balloon.

tauri.note: tauri-plugin-notification.

features.title: Drag and drop with other apps
features.description: Accepts drops from, and drags to, the file manager and other apps.

egui.note: Receives dropped files; dragging out of the app is not built in.

gtk.note: GtkDragSource and GtkDropTarget.

slint.note: DragArea/DropArea work inside the application; cross-app drag and drop awaits winit support.

qt.note: QDrag and drop events with MIME data.

tauri.note: Drag-drop events for files dropped on a window; dragging out needs a community plugin.

features.title: Multiple windows
features.description: Opens additional native top-level windows.

egui.note: Viewports open native windows on desktop backends.

gtk.note: GtkWindow.

slint.note: Each component with a Window root can be shown separately.

qt.note: Any top-level QWidget.

tauri.note: WebviewWindow; each window hosts a webview.

features.title: System credential store
features.description: Keychain, Windows Credential Manager or Secret Service for tokens and passwords.

egui.note: keyring crate.

gtk.note: keyring or oo7 (Secret Service; libsecret's protocol).

slint.note: keyring crate.

qt.note: Third-party QtKeychain.

tauri.note: keyring crate; the official Stronghold plugin is its own encrypted vault, not the OS store.

features.title: Badge on the app icon
features.description: A count or label on the app's icon in the macOS Dock, the Windows taskbar or a Linux dock.

egui.note: No eframe API. Needs NSDockTile (objc2), ITaskbarList3 overlay icons (windows crate) or the Unity LauncherEntry D-Bus signal on Linux.

gtk.note: No GTK API. On Linux, docks such as Dash to Dock and KDE Plasma read the com.canonical.Unity.LauncherEntry D-Bus signal, which gio can emit; Windows and macOS need native calls.

slint.note: No Slint API; native code can use the window handle from the winit accessor.

qt.note: QGuiApplication::setBadgeNumber since Qt 6.5 (Dock, taskbar). Measured here: Windows 6.8 and macOS 6.12 have it; Ubuntu 24.04's Qt 6.4 does not.

tauri.note: set_badge_count on macOS and Linux (Unity LauncherEntry, needs the .desktop name and a dock that reads it), set_badge_label on macOS; Windows has set_overlay_icon (an icon, not a number).

features.title: Progress on the app icon
features.description: A progress bar drawn over the taskbar button or Dock icon, for downloads or exports.

egui.note: No eframe API; ITaskbarList3, NSDockTile or the Unity LauncherEntry signal.

gtk.note: No GTK API; on Linux the Unity LauncherEntry signal carries progress.

slint.note: No Slint API; native code through the winit window handle.

qt.note: QWinTaskbarProgress went away with Qt Windows Extras in Qt 6; use ITaskbarList3 or NSDockTile directly.

tauri.note: set_progress_bar. On macOS and Linux the bar is app-wide; Linux needs a libunity-aware dock.

features.title: Request attention
features.description: Bounce the Dock icon, flash the taskbar button or mark the window urgent.

egui.note: ViewportCommand::RequestUserAttention (winit). Wayland needs the compositor's xdg_activation_v1.

gtk.note: No cross-platform GTK 4 call. X11 has gdk_x11_surface_set_urgency_hint (deprecated in 4.18); Windows and macOS need FlashWindowEx or NSApplication from native code.

slint.note: No Slint property; winit's request_user_attention is reachable through the unstable winit accessor (unstable-winit-030 feature).

qt.note: QApplication::alert: Dock bounce on macOS, taskbar flash on Windows, 'demands attention' on X11.

tauri.note: request_user_attention (critical or informational on macOS; one level on Linux).

features.title: Dock menu or jump list
features.description: Extra entries when right-clicking the app's Dock icon or taskbar button.

egui.note: No eframe API. macOS needs an NSApplicationDelegate (applicationDockMenu:); Windows jump lists need ICustomDestinationList. Linux .desktop Actions are static packaging.

gtk.note: No GTK 4 API. Linux .desktop Actions are static packaging.

slint.note: No Slint API.

qt.note: QMenu::setAsDockMenu on macOS. Windows jump lists (QWinJumpList) were removed with Qt Windows Extras in Qt 6.

tauri.note: No Dock menu or jump list API in Tauri 2.12; Linux .desktop Actions via the bundler.

features.title: Menu-bar or background-only app
features.description: Run without a Dock icon or taskbar button, e.g. an app that lives in the tray.

egui.note: macOS: winit ActivationPolicy::Accessory through NativeOptions::event_loop_builder; Windows: ViewportBuilder::with_taskbar(false); Linux has no equivalent.

gtk.note: No GTK API. macOS: LSUIElement in Info.plist; Windows: extended window styles from native code.

slint.note: Through winit: BackendSelector::with_winit_event_loop_builder for the macOS activation policy; window attributes for Windows.

qt.note: Qt::Tool windows have no taskbar button; macOS hides the Dock icon with LSUIElement in Info.plist.

tauri.note: set_activation_policy / set_dock_visibility on macOS; skipTaskbar on Windows and Linux.

features.title: Tray clicks and menu
features.description: React to clicks on the tray icon, not only to its menu.

egui.note: tray-icon crate. Its ksni backend (no GTK 3) reports clicks on Linux; the default AppIndicator backend does not. Needs a StatusNotifier host on Linux.

gtk.note: tray-icon with the ksni and muda-gtk4 features, or ksni directly; GTK 3-based AppIndicator libraries cannot load into a GTK 4 process.

slint.note: SystemTrayIcon clicked(): left-click on Windows; on macOS only when no menu is attached; Linux via StatusNotifierItem Activate.

qt.note: QSystemTrayIcon::activated with the click reason; Linux uses StatusNotifierItem or XEmbed.

tauri.note: Tray events on Windows and macOS; on Linux the AppIndicator backend emits no click events, only the menu works.

features.title: Global keyboard shortcuts
features.description: A hotkey that reaches the app while another app is focused.

egui.note: global-hotkey crate: Windows, macOS, Linux X11 only. Wayland needs the GlobalShortcuts portal.

gtk.note: global-hotkey on Windows/macOS/X11; on Wayland the GlobalShortcuts portal (e.g. ashpd crate).

slint.note: global-hotkey crate: Windows, macOS, Linux X11 only.

qt.note: No Qt API; third-party QHotkey (X11 only on Linux).

tauri.note: global-shortcut plugin, built on global-hotkey: Linux X11 only.

features.title: Start at login
features.description: Register the app to start when the user logs in.

egui.note: auto-launch crate: Run registry key, LaunchAgent or login item, XDG autostart or systemd.

gtk.note: auto-launch crate; sandboxed Linux apps use the Background portal.

slint.note: auto-launch crate.

qt.note: No Qt API; write the Run key, a LaunchAgent plist or an XDG autostart .desktop file.

tauri.note: autostart plugin (wraps auto-launch).

features.title: Single instance
features.description: A second launch hands its arguments to the running app and exits.

egui.note: Not built in; e.g. the single-instance or interprocess crates.

gtk.note: GApplication is unique per application ID and forwards arguments; documented through the D-Bus session bus on Linux, not documented for Windows and macOS.

slint.note: Not built in; e.g. the single-instance or interprocess crates.

qt.note: Not in Qt 6; third-party SingleApplication, or QLocalServer by hand.

tauri.note: single-instance plugin, which also routes deep links.

features.title: URL schemes and file associations
features.description: Open myapp:// links and double-clicked documents in the app.

egui.note: Registration is packaging (Info.plist, registry, .desktop). Windows and Linux pass the URL as an argument; macOS delivers an Apple Event that needs your own NSApplicationDelegate.

gtk.note: GApplication open signal with the HANDLES_OPEN flag; registration through the .desktop file on Linux. Not documented for macOS.

slint.note: As for egui: packaging plus arguments; macOS needs a custom application delegate.

qt.note: macOS: QFileOpenEvent for files and URLs. Windows/Linux: registration by the installer, URL arrives as an argument.

tauri.note: deep-link plugin (runtime registration on Windows/Linux, bundle-only on macOS) plus bundler fileAssociations.

features.title: Installers and updates
features.description: Official tooling to produce installers and deliver updates.

egui.note: General Rust packagers such as cargo-packager.

gtk.note: Flatpak and distro packages on Linux. On Windows/macOS the GTK runtime must be collected and bundled by the app; this repository copies the MSYS2 runtime.

slint.note: General Rust packagers.

qt.note: windeployqt/macdeployqt collect the runtime; installers via Qt Installer Framework. No built-in updater.

tauri.note: Built-in bundler (MSI/NSIS, .app/.dmg, deb/rpm/AppImage) and an official updater plugin.

features.title: Other targets
features.description: Platforms beyond desktop.

slint.text: Embedded MCUs, Linux KMS, Android, WebAssembly

qt.text: Android, iOS (Qt Quick preferred there), embedded Linux

features.title: Rust API
features.description: How a Rust application talks to the toolkit.

tauri.text: Rust core; UI in web code

features.title: Licence
features.description: Toolkit licence (dependencies differ).
